data.turoyo: B iḏoṯa gqayšo i zəbdo, yaʕni u məšḥo, i zəbdo, gmaləmola, gmašəġola w gəmmalḥola w gmaḥtola b səfoqo. <...>
data.translation: Mit den Händen schöpft sie die Butter ab, sammelt sie, wäscht sie, salzt sie und legt sie in ein Gefäß. <...>

rationale: New Infectum box; singular female agent and suffixed butter patient.

data.turoyo: <...> bəṯr mu məloḥawo ksaymila maye w malḥo, ġer manək, w kmaydi af falqani, kmaḥtənne b tanagaye w kkufxi i maye w malḥayo aʕlayye <...>

rationale: New Infinitiv box, provisionally classified; salting event in a temporal nominal phrase.

summary: The new Infectum forms are transitive: a feminine 3sg subject salts butter with suffix -la, and a 3pl subject salts cheese with -la. They supply the missing box beside the inherited Infectum-wa.
məloḥawo in bəṯr mu məloḥawo denotes the salting event and is provisionally placed in Infinitiv. -awo belongs to the nominal expression; it is not finite -wa.

The sequence in JTM 1.1/83 distinguishes salting the cheese from subsequently making and pouring a salt solution. It supports 'to salt'; no distinct sense 'to pickle' is inferred from the procedure or the inherited uncertain translation.

The inherited etymological question about direct verbal inheritance versus derivation from the salt noun remains open. The observed II morphology alone cannot decide historical derivation. No light-verb collocation of mlḥ is present.
Confirm məloḥawo as the Infinitiv of II mmaləḥ rather than an independently derived action noun, and establish its base vocalism.
Can the inherited 'to pickle' gloss be supported by a separate context? These new records directly attest salting; they do not justify deleting the existing gloss.
Butter and cheese join the inherited meat patient. These food changes extend the same salting event, without a new sense.
